meta.phase-name: Contract-Backed Content Pack Registry for Editor Surfaces

phase-plan.purpose: Make the content editor, docs-site content pack pages, and future Payload CRUD flows consume a canonical pack registry exported by the engine contracts layer instead of ad hoc filesystem scans or duplicated pack lists.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: engine-side pack metadata registry, docs-site API consumption of that registry, content-pack surface alignment, and planning/docs updates. Out of scope: full Payload collection migration and publish workflow implementation.

file.description: Canonical runtime contract export layer; should publish pack metadata for editor consumption.
Current content-pack API uses filesystem scans; should switch to canonical engine metadata.
Content app summary page should reflect contract-backed pack metadata instead of implicit file counts only.
Repo architecture doc should record the editor/runtime contract boundary and next execution phases.

task.description: Define a canonical pack registry shape in the engine contracts layer with pack ids, runtime export names, schema/source/runtime file metadata, and structural counts.
Make docs-site content-pack API and content app consume the engine registry instead of filesystem-only scans.
Record the editor/runtime/publish boundary in architecture docs so later Payload and delivery phases build on the same contract.

questions.question: Should Payload collections mirror pack rows one collection per pack, or should drafts first land in a generic pack-document/revision model before collection-level CRUD is expanded?

decision.summary: Before changing database strategy, the repo needs one engine-authored registry that defines what a pack is and how editor surfaces discover it.
decision.impact: Prevents docs-site, Payload, and runtime delivery code from each inventing their own pack catalogs.

suggestion.gap: REQ-89/90 do not yet state that editor surfaces must discover pack definitions from canonical engine contract metadata.
suggestion.proposal: Add a requirement that authoring/editor UIs consume a shared pack registry exported by the engine contracts layer, with draft DBs publishing back into contract-shaped runtime artifacts.
